newsitem.title: USA: Ziff-Davis acquiring stake in Herring Communications.
newsitem.headline: Ziff-Davis acquiring stake in Herring Communications.

text.p: Japanese computer power Softbank Corp.'s Ziff-Davis computer publishing arm has agreed to acquire a minority stake in Herring Communications Inc., which organises conferences and publishes the irreverent Red Herring high-tech business magazine.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed, including how big a piece of privately held Herring Ziff-Davis Publishing Co. is buying.

Herring Communications, which announced the deal Tuesday, focuses on technology and venture capital markets. The monthly Red Herring is considered a bible for venture capitalists and those involved in high-tech initial public offerings.

Ziff-Davis's investment marks the first infusion of outside capital into 4-year-old Herring Communications, said Herring President Christopher Alden. He said a detailed agreement on the relationship between the companies was being negotiated.

"What we also get is distribution, production, credibility and access to media buyers," Alden said, referring to the broad network of computer publications and investments in Internet firms under the Ziff-Davis and Softbank umbrella.

In addition to owning the world's largest computer-related publishing operation, Tokyo-based Softbank distributes software, owns a piece of the popular Yahoo! Inc. Internet search operation and Kingston Technology, the world's largest maker of computer memory products.

Herring Communications, which organises nine conferences in the United States and Europe on investing in high-tech companies, was profitable last year, according to Alden, and the capital will be used for further expansion.

In addition to the conferences and the magazine, Herring has launched a quarterly for Internet entrepreneurs called "Hits," published a book and launched a weekly online newsletter in partnership with Netscape Communications Corp.

The company also aims to expand into daily news on the high-tech and venture capital markets, and to establish a research arm providing detailed strategic and financial information on emerging technologies and companies.

Ziff-Davis Chief Executive Officer Eric Hippeau will join Red Herring Editor In Chief Tony Perkins, Alden and Ronald Conway, a business strategy executive at CBT Systems, on Herring's board of directors.
Herring, which currently employs 63 people and plans to increase its staff to more than 100, will produce content under its brand name for the Ziff-Davis online news service ZDNet.
The Ziff-Davis Web site also publishes on-line editions of its computing publications, which include PC Magazine, PC Week, MacWeek and Internet User.
Alden said there will also be possibilities for cooperation with Softbank's Comdex trade show group, which runs major computer industry conferences.
Herring Communications does not publish its financial figures, but industry sources said the fast-growing company's revenues doubled to around $6.8 million in 1996 from $2.8 million in 1995.

"Our goal is to be an integrated media company that cleverly sells information and advertising space across different media platforms," Red Herring co-founder and editor Perkins wrote in May's edition.

Alden said the Ziff-Davis deal would not rule out further investments, but said that was not Herring's intention at the moment. He added that the deal could better position the company for an initial public offering.

"Clearly, one of our strategies has been growth. We have invested as much as we could on growing the company," said Alden, who made the announcement formally at the company's Web Markets West conference here.
